answer: An attacker therefore has to keep each extra identity continuously active for 11 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. The harbor counter is kept in spiral and ember exposes each reset. A bond is refunded only after 11 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 3 epochs. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
